biothings.name: endometrial undifferentiated carcinoma
biothings.definition: A primary carcinoma of the endometrium characterized by the presence of malignant cells that lack evidence of differentiation. [NCIT:C40156]
biothings.synonyms: endometrial undifferentiated carcinoma, undifferentiated endometrial carcinoma

biothings.name: endometrial carcinoma
biothings.definition: A malignant tumor arising from the epithelium that lines the cavity of the uterine body. The vast majority of endometrial carcinomas are adenocarcinomas; squamous cell and adenosquamous carcinomas represent a minority of the cases. Endometrioid adenocarcinoma is the most frequently seen variant of endometrial adenocarcinoma. Uterine bleeding is an initial clinical sign. The prognosis depends on the stage of the tumor, the depth of myometrial wall invasion, and the degree of differentiation. [NCIT:C7558]
biothings.synonyms: carcinoma of endometrium, carcinoma of the endometrium, carcinoma, endometrial, malignant, endometrial carcinoma, endometrial carcinoma (disease), endometrium carcinoma

biothings.name: endometrial adenosquamous carcinoma
biothings.definition: A rare endometrial carcinoma characterized by the presence of both malignant glandular and malignant squamous cellular components. [NCIT:P378]
biothings.synonyms: endometrial adenosquamous carcinoma, endometrium adenosquamous carcinoma

biothings.name: endometrial transitional cell carcinoma
biothings.definition: A rare primary carcinoma of the endometrium characterized by the presence of malignant epithelial cells resembling urothelial transitional cells. The malignant transitional cells constitute at least 90% of the tumor cells. [NCIT:C40154]

biothings.name: uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma
biothings.definition: A endometrial carcinoma (disease) that involves the body of uterus. [MONDO:patterns/location]
biothings.synonyms: body of uterus endometrial carcinoma (disease), endometrial carcinoma (disease) of body of uterus

opentargets.name: endometrial carcinoma
opentargets.description: A malignant tumor arising from the epithelium that lines the cavity of the uterine body. The vast majority of endometrial carcinomas are adenocarcinomas; squamous cell and adenosquamous carcinomas represent a minority of the cases. Endometrioid adenocarcinoma is the most frequently seen variant of endometrial adenocarcinoma. Uterine bleeding is an initial clinical sign. The prognosis depends on the stage of the tumor, the depth of myometrial wall invasion, and the degree of differentiation.

opentargets.name: endometrial cancer
opentargets.description: Primary or metastatic malignant neoplasm involving the endometrium (mucous membrane that lines the endometrial cavity).

opentargets.name: endometrial serous adenocarcinoma
opentargets.description: A high grade, aggressive adenocarcinoma arising from the endometrium. It is characterized by the presence of complex papillary patterns with cellular budding. Atypical mitoses, necrosis, and psammoma bodies may be present. It is classified as type II endometrial carcinoma and it is not associated with endometrial hyperplasia. It tends to invade deeply into the myometrium and spreads into the lymphatic vessels. Patients frequently present with spread of the tumor beyond the uterus at the time of diagnosis. The prognosis is usually poor.

opentargets.name: uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma
opentargets.description: A endometrial carcinoma (disease) that involves the body of uterus.

opentargets.name: endometrial disorder
opentargets.description: A non-neoplastic or neoplastic disorder that affects the endometrium. Representative examples include endometritis, endometrial hyperplasia, and endometrial carcinoma.
